[[817.6]] 231a. ROBERT HOOKE AN THEODOR HAAK FÜR LEIBNIZ

[[817.7]] [London, 13. April 1681.] [228a.]

[[817.19]] S^#'r

[[817.20]] I am extreamly pleasd to find soe excellent a Person as the Learned world must Acknowledg

[[817.21]] M^#'r Leibnitz to concur in the same opinion w^#'t^#'h me that A language somew^#'t Like that of

[[817.22]] y^#'e Bishop of Chester would be of use for the Promotion of Science. It has been Long my

[[817.23]] Judgment, and that founded upon undenyable principles from w^#'c^#'h I cannot Recede that this

[[817.24]] Language would be of much greater use then the world has conceived, though I have hitherto

[[817.25]] had the Ill fortune scarcly to meet w^#'t^#'h one man (except himself) whom I can persuade to concurr

[[817.26]] w^#'t^#'h me and that the Greatest number Look upon it only as a chymera and at best but a

[[817.27]] Supplement for Latine in the inner parts of Europe or for the Lingua franca in the maritime, yet

[[817.28]] my aymes have Always been much higher viz. to make it not only usefull for Expressing and

[[817.29]] Remembring of things and notions but to Direct Regulate assist and even necessitate and

[[818.1]] compell the mind to find out and comprehent whatsoever is knowable. And to make it an

[[818.2]] Instrument which being actuated by the power of the mind shall most certainly produce the

[[818.3]] Desired effect or plainly show the Impossibility thereof; especially in all those subjects where

[[818.4]] y^#'e use of it may be free and where interest and Authority doe not Intercept the Regular Course

[[818.5]] thereof, which I conceive to be the great antagonists which may impede its progress, preposession

[[818.6]] may clogg it but it will get through safe and well: not withstanding. It may therefore not

[[818.7]] unfitly be called the Algebra of Algebras or the Science of methods, which every one that now

[[818.8]] Invents a particular method does somew^#'t participate but comes short of the full perfection and

[[818.9]] best of that kind, at Least if he Light on it he knows not how he came by it nor can he prove that

[[818.10]] tis soe and not otherwise. Any thing therefore that M^#'r Leibnitz knows that will promote this end

[[818.11]] will be highly acceptable if he please to communicate it and shall be acknowledged as his. The

[[818.12]] Great Difficulty lyes in the media but the Generall method will not only plainely show what

[[818.13]] those are but the way of attaining them, but this is not to be done in many subjects but w^#'t^#'h much

[[818.14]] exercise of the method and there is a subordination and positure in the subjects of Inquiry

[[818.15]] themselves, and therefore the first Alphabet or those which may be called the Symbols are first

[[818.16]] to be understood, then those which may be called the Syllables then the words then sentences or

[[818.17]] propositions etc. nor is it to be imagined a Scollar in this art shall at first sight read perfectly

[[818.18]] But must with Labour and Patience proceed methodically, and goe by steps from subject to

[[818.19]] subject as Nature has placed them in order, and then tis not to be doubted but the Soule of man

[[818.20]] may be carryed to the highest step of knowledge and comprehend scientifically whatever is

[[818.21]] made capable of knowing. To compleat which the united Labours of many will be necessary

[[818.22]] and of such as are fitly qualifyed and those often Meeting and Debating together, and exerting

[[818.23]] their utmost abilitys in A right way. But where are these to be found. Either will or ability or

[[818.24]] opportunity or some other necessary concomitant is found wanting. Soe that I fear this may be

[[818.25]] seen in Speculation but twill be very difficult to bring it into act, and Every one must be content

[[818.26]] to improve himself soe far as he can in the Disquisition on this or that subject he has most

[[818.27]] present need of knowing. I question not but M^#'r Leibnitz may have many of these specimina by

[[818.28]] him and therefore I doe heartily wish you could prevaile w^#'t^#'h him to Communicate some of these

[[818.29]] which would be a means to persuade severall yet incredulous of the possibility of such a

[[818.30]] Science: for my own part I Should very gladly contribute my Indeavours towards this end but

[[818.31]] the Scarcity of Persons to converse w^#'t^#'h concerning it does almost Discourage me. But the

[[819.1]] concurrence and confirmation of soe excellent a Person as Mon^#'r Leibnitz would be very

[[819.2]] prevalent for making Proselyts. Darunter von Hookes Hand: concerning M^#'r Leibnitz his Dessigne for Universall Language or Characters sent by M^#'r Haak to M^#'r Leibnitz May 15, 1681.
